answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a bonded identity island: each new agent must lock a stake that any peer can slash after a duplicate is proven. Reputation follows a single thread per identity, so clones start at zero and must pay real compute plus elapsed time to be trusted. An attacker spinning a thousand sock puppets therefore funds a thousand bonds and sustains proofs for each, a cost that grows linearly while rewards shrink. Honest newcomers show up like a comet — briefly bright, priced low until history accumulates.
